# Blueprint design system

React components and semantic design tokens aligned with the **Blueprint** Figma component library. Components use a `Bp` prefix and named exports; props are intended to stay close to the design system for a predictable handoff from design to code.

**Documentation:** browse components, props, and examples in the [published Storybook](https://ux.netapp.com/storybook/blueprint/).

**Repository:** [github.com/NetApp/blueprint](https://github.com/NetApp/blueprint)

**Package registry:** the `@netapp/blueprint` npm package is available from:
- GitHub Packages: [npm.pkg.github.com](https://npm.pkg.github.com/)
- NetApp repo: [npm.repo.eng.netapp.com](https://npm.repo.eng.netapp.com)

**MCP server:** teach your agents, such as Cursor, about the components through the [Blueprint MCP server](https://ux.netapp.com/blueprint/mcp).

**For designers:** Figma canvas agent skills are in [`designer-agent/DESIGNERS.md`](designer-agent/DESIGNERS.md).

Library maintenance, CI, Figma agent workflows, and contributor setup are documented in [`docs/maintaining-the-library.md`](docs/maintaining-the-library.md).

## Requirements

- **React 18+** (and `react-dom` 18+) as peer dependencies
- **`react-aria-components` 1.17+** as a peer dependency — Blueprint uses it internally for accessible overlays, menus, dialogs, and tooltips; install it alongside Blueprint in your app
- **ESM** package; bundlers should resolve `import` from `@netapp/blueprint` and subpaths normally

## Quick start

1. Install the package (and its peer dependencies):

```bash
npm install --save @netapp/blueprint react-aria-components
```
or, if you're developing within a secure NetApp network:
~~~bash
npm install --save --registry=https://npm.repo.eng.netapp.com @netapp/blueprint react-aria-components
~~~

2. Import components from the package root or the explicit React subpath:

```ts
import { BpButton, BpTextField } from "@netapp/blueprint";
// or
import { BpButton } from "@netapp/blueprint/react";
```

3. Load Blueprint CSS once in your app shell — production apps use `css`; exploration prototypes use `prototype` ([exploration prototypes](#exploration-prototypes)):

```ts
import "@netapp/blueprint/prototype";
```

4. Use components in your app:

```tsx
<BpButton appearance="solid">Save</BpButton>
<BpButton appearance="outline">Cancel</BpButton>
```

**Notes:**

- `@netapp/blueprint/react` is also exported if you prefer an explicit React-only subpath.
- `@netapp/blueprint/css` includes component rules and the full token bundle.
- `@netapp/blueprint/tokens.css` is the **full patched token monolith** (primitives, layout, semantic theme, variants, and `bp-*` font-smoothing) — not semantic tokens only. Do not load it together with split layers (`layout.css`, `text-styles.css`, etc.).
- Blueprint styles include scoped text smoothing defaults for `bp-*` component roots on macOS (`-webkit-font-smoothing` / `-moz-osx-font-smoothing`). `layout.css` includes the same block. Override font-smoothing in app CSS only if needed.

### Exploration prototypes

For discussion or early validation (not production-bound work), import `@netapp/blueprint/prototype` instead of `css`. It loads Blueprint styles with **concept fidelity** enabled (`data-fidelity="concept"`) so reviewers see grayscale styling and a fixed “not for production” banner.

Set the attribute on `<html>` in your shell to avoid a brief flash before JavaScript runs:

```html
<html data-fidelity="concept">
```

```ts
import "@netapp/blueprint/prototype";
import { BpButton } from "@netapp/blueprint";
```

See [`docs/ai-layout-guidelines.md`](docs/ai-layout-guidelines.md) for layout patterns. Do not import `@netapp/blueprint/concept.css` unless you need the overlay alone (Storybook fidelity toggle or advanced setups).

### CSS import scenarios

Production apps: `@netapp/blueprint/css`. Exploration prototypes: `@netapp/blueprint/prototype`.

| Scenario | Import |
| --- | --- |
| Full Blueprint app | `@netapp/blueprint/css` |
| Exploration prototype (concept fidelity) | `@netapp/blueprint/prototype` |
| Tokens only (no component rules) | `@netapp/blueprint/tokens.css` |
| Styles needed by Blueprint components | `@netapp/blueprint/layout.css` |

## Subpath exports

| Import path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `@netapp/blueprint` | Default entry; React components and related types |
| `@netapp/blueprint/react` | Same React surface, explicit subpath |
| `@netapp/blueprint/i18n` | Locale provider for library-owned default strings |
| `@netapp/blueprint/icons` | Icon metadata / SVG helpers |
| `@netapp/blueprint/icons/react` | Lazy `BpIconByName`, static per-icon components (`IcCloseIcon`, …) |
| `@netapp/blueprint/format` | Formatting utilities |
| `@netapp/blueprint/css` | Full stylesheet (component rules + token bundle) |
| `@netapp/blueprint/prototype` | Exploration prototypes — concept fidelity on by default |
| `@netapp/blueprint/concept.css` | Concept fidelity layer only (advanced; use with `data-fidelity="concept"`) |
| `@netapp/blueprint/tokens.css` | Token monolith only — see [CSS import scenarios](#css-import-scenarios) |
| `@netapp/blueprint/layout.css` | Typography, spacing, and layout tokens |
| `@netapp/blueprint/text-styles.css` | `.text-*` typography utility classes |
| `@netapp/blueprint/tokens.json` | Full token metadata (JSON) |

When adding new components inside this repo, export wiring is documented in [`docs/package-exports.md`](docs/package-exports.md).

## Styling and layout

- **App shell first:** when generating a new Blueprint app or route, start with `BpPageShell` + `BpAppShell`. Include a top `BpHeader` (hamburger opens `BpMainNav`), and a `BpServiceNav` inside `BpMainRegion` before adding page content. This keeps app chrome, offsets, and navigation consistent across generated pages.
- For dashboards, tables, forms, and side panels, Blueprint provides layout primitives (see [`docs/ai-layout-guidelines.md`](docs/ai-layout-guidelines.md)) so pages share consistent spacing and responsive behavior.

Load Blueprint CSS once in your app entry before this scaffold: production → `@netapp/blueprint/css`; exploration prototypes → `@netapp/blueprint/prototype` (see [Exploration prototypes](#exploration-prototypes)). App shells clear the browser default `body` margin automatically — no extra reset CSS is required.

Copy-paste starter scaffold:

```tsx
import { useState, type ReactNode } from "react";
import {
  BpAppShell,
  BpContentRegion,
  BpHeader,
  BpInline,
  BpMainNav,
  BpMainRegion,
  BpPageShell,
  BpServiceNav,
  BpStack,
  type BpMainNavCategory,
  type BpServiceNavItemData,
} from "@netapp/blueprint";

const navCategories: BpMainNavCategory[] = [
  { id: "favorites", label: "Favorites" },
  { id: "home", label: "Home" },
  {
    id: "storage",
    label: "Storage",
    icon: "ic_object_storage",
    services: [
      { id: "systems", label: "Systems", description: "Manage storage systems." },
      { id: "volumes", label: "Volumes", description: "Review volume health and capacity." },
    ],
  },
];

const serviceNavItems: BpServiceNavItemData[] = [
  { id: "overview", label: "Overview" },
  { id: "health", label: "Health" },
  { id: "configuration", label: "Configuration" },
];

export function BlueprintAppScaffold({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  const [activeControlId, setActiveControlId] = useState<string | null>(null);

  return (
    <BpPageShell>
      <BpAppShell
        header={
          <BpHeader.Prototype
            activeControlId={activeControlId}
            onActiveControlChange={setActiveControlId}
            mainNavPanel={
              <BpMainNav
                open={activeControlId === "main-nav"}
                onOpenChange={(open) => setActiveControlId(open ? "main-nav" : null)}
                categories={navCategories}
                activeCategoryId="storage"
                selectedServiceId="systems"
              />
            }
          />
        }
        content={
          <BpMainRegion>
              <BpInline wrap={false} space="0" style={{ alignItems: "stretch", width: "100%" }}>
                <BpServiceNav serviceLabel="Systems" items={serviceNavItems} selectedItemId="overview" />
                <BpStack grow space="0" style={{ minWidth: 0 }}>
                  <BpContentRegion width="full" center={false}>
                    <BpStack space="300">{children}</BpStack>
                  </BpContentRegion>
                </BpStack>
              </BpInline>
            </BpMainRegion>
        }
      />
    </BpPageShell>
  );
}
```

**Typography:** canonical text styles are emitted as `--text-*` variables in `tokens.css`. Example: Figma `Title/20 . Semibold` maps to `--text-title-20-size`, `--text-title-20-line-height`, `--text-letter-spacing`, and `--font-weight-semibold`.

## Internationalization (i18n)

Library-owned default strings are resolved through the Blueprint locale provider:

```ts
import { setBlueprintLocaleProvider } from "@netapp/blueprint/i18n";
```

Set or update your provider when the application locale changes. If your provider returns `undefined` for a key, built-in English defaults are used. Labels and copy you pass explicitly via props or `children` stay under your control.

## Agent setup

After `npm install @netapp/blueprint`, the package ships a versioned agent bundle (`@netapp/blueprint/agent/*`) with the same manifests the [hosted MCP server](https://ux.netapp.com/blueprint/mcp) serves — start at `agent/index.json`, then read `guidelines-layout` and related entries from `agent/manifests/docs.json` (see [`docs/ai-layout-guidelines.md`](docs/ai-layout-guidelines.md)). Export paths, guideline ids, and MCP setup: [`docs/package-exports.md`](docs/package-exports.md).
